rows.text:
• Classification of elements into different groups
• Periods

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ All transition elements are d-block, and all d-block elements are transition elements. ✅ All transition elements belong to d-block, but Zn, Cd, and Hg are d-block elements that are NOT transition elements because their d-subshell is completely filled (d¹⁰) in ground state and common +2 oxidation state.  ·  ❌ Hydrogen is an alkali metal because it sits in Group 1. ✅ Hydrogen has an 1s¹ configuration but is a non-metal with high ionization enthalpy (1312 kJ/mol), forming covalent bonds and H⁻ hydride ions.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Atomic number (Z), representing nuclear charge, uniquely dictates chemical identity and electron configurations.  ·  Half-filled (p³, d⁵, f⁷) and fully filled (p⁶, d¹⁰, f¹⁴) subshells possess maximum symmetry and exchange energy stability.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Worked: identify given → pick sub-concept → apply standard form → check units / edges.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### 1. Structural Architecture of the Modern Periodic Table (Bohr's Long Form)  ·  • Based on Moseley's Modern Periodic Law: The physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers (nuclear charge, Z).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: The periodic table represents the direct geometric visualization of quantum mechanical energy level solutions (Aufbau principle and Hund's rule).  ·  Poor shielding ability follows the order: s > p > d > f; this fundamental rule dictates both the inert pair effect and lanthanide contraction.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: state + explain the main idea of "Classification of elements into different groups, periods…" with one example.  ·  compare "Classification of elements into different groups" with the related idea from a neighbouring unit.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: ❌ Helium belongs to p-block because it sits in Group 18. ✅ Helium has the valence configuration 1s² (s-block), but is placed in Group 18 above p-block noble gases due to its completely filled valence shell and inert noble chemical properties.  ·  ❌ Fluorine has the highest electron gain enthalpy (electron affinity) in the periodic table. ✅ Chlorine (Cl) has higher negative electron gain enthalpy than Fluorine (-349 kJ/mol vs -328 kJ/mol) because Fluorine's 2p subshell is very small and compact, causing strong inter-electronic repulsions that hinder incoming electrons.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: • Consists of 7 horizontal rows called **Periods** and 18 vertical columns called **Groups** (IUPAC 1 to 18).  ·  • **Period 1:** 2 elements (H, He) — shortest period (fills 1s subshell).  ·  • **Periods 2 & 3:** 8 elements each (Li–Ne, Na–Ar) — short periods (fill 2s, 2p and 3s, 3p subshells).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Ionization enthalpy always increases monotonically across a period from left to right. ✅ Exceptions exist: Beryllium (1s² 2s²) has higher IE₁ than Boron (1s² 2s² 2p¹) because 2s electrons penetrate closer to the nucleus and are fully paired; Nitrogen (2s² 2p³) has higher IE₁ than Oxygen (2s² 2p⁴) due to the extra…  ·  ❌ Lanthanum (₅₇La) and Actinium (₈₉Ac) are f-block elements. ✅ La and Ac are d-block elements (outer configuration 5d¹ 6s² and 6d¹ 7s²). The f-block begins with Cerium (₅₈Ce) and Thorium (₉₀Th).  ·  ❌ Lanthanide contraction means the atoms expand down the group. ✅ Contraction means atomic/ionic radii decrease steadily across the 4f series from Ce to Lu due to poor shielding by diffuse 4f orbitals.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Copper, Silver, and Gold are non-transition metals because their ground state is d¹⁰. ✅ They are transition metals because their common oxidation states have partially filled d-orbitals: Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹, Au³⁺ is 5d⁸.  ·  ❌ Graphite is an insulator like other non-metals. ✅ Graphite conducts electricity along its hexagonal sheets due to free delocalized π-electrons resulting from sp² hybridization.  ·  ❌ All oxides of metals are basic. ✅ Most are basic, but metal oxides with high oxidation states are acidic (e.g., CrO₃ with Cr⁶⁺, Mn₂O₇ with Mn⁷⁺), and some are amphoteric (Al₂O₃, ZnO, PbO, SnO).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Coinage metals include Zinc, Cadmium, and Mercury. ✅ Coinage metals are strictly Group 11 (Cu, Ag, Au). Group 12 (Zn, Cd, Hg) are Volatile Metals.  ·  ❌ Mercury dissolves all metals to form amalgams. ✅ Mercury does NOT amalgamate with Iron (Fe), Platinum (Pt), or Tungsten (W); therefore, mercury is safely shipped and stored in iron flasks.  ·  Write the complete electronic configuration of Cu (Z=29), Cr (Z=24), Fe³⁺ (Z=26), and Ce⁴⁺ (Z=58).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Explain why Zn²⁺ salts are colorless and diamagnetic, whereas Cu²⁺ salts are blue and paramagnetic.  ·  Calculate the magnetic moment (spin-only) for Fe²⁺ (3d⁶) and Mn²⁺ (3d⁵).  ·  State Modern Periodic Law and describe how Moseley proved that atomic number is more fundamental than atomic mass.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Discuss the causes and three major consequences of Lanthanide Contraction on 4d/5d transition elements.  ·  Explain why the first ionization enthalpy of Nitrogen is greater than that of Oxygen, but the second ionization enthalpy of Oxygen is greater than that of Nitrogen.  ·  Give reasons: (a) Why are alkali metals stored under kerosene? (b) Why is Lithium the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution?
